Paper: A Survey of LLM-based Multi-agent Systems in Medicine (also arXiv 1883)
Agent Architecture: Taxonomy: team composition, medical knowledge augmentation, agent interaction
Headline Result: Proposes a 3-axis taxonomy and lists open problems
Gap It Leaves: No protocol for measuring role fidelity, no standard for MAS evaluation

Agent Architecture: Agents each build a syllogistic logic tree (major premise, minor premise, conclusion)
Interaction Protocol: Multi-round graph-guided discussion; premise-level alignment; contradiction resolution
Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy vs single-agent and role-based MAS
Headline Result: SOTA on MedDDx and medical QA; scales across open and commercial backbones
Gap It Leaves: No real clinical data; no cost reporting; no longitudinal revision

Paper: An Adaptive Multi-Agent LLM-Based Clinical Decision Support System
Agent Architecture: Retrieval agent (BioBERT vector DB) + web-evidence agent + fusion agent + adaptive optimisation loop on low confidence
Interaction Protocol: Adaptive retry loop when confidence is low
Stated Limitation: Evaluated only on MCQ; no clinician study
Gap It Leaves: Confidence loop is heuristic; no calibration guarantee; no cost analysis

Agent Architecture: Single-agent first pass + multi-agent consultation only for escalated cases
Interaction Protocol: Conformal confidence triage -> escalate hard cases
Headline Result: >50% cost reduction at comparable accuracy; MAS up to 50x slower than single call
Stated Limitation: Two-stage triage: decides whether to escalate but not whom to convene
Gap It Leaves: MCQA only; no test-ordering or resource constraints

Paper: DDO: Dual-Decision Optimization for LLM-Based Medical Consultation
Agent Architecture: Inquiry agent (RL-trained) + diagnosis agent; decoupled objectives
Stated Limitation: Requires local model training; incompatible with API LLMs; hard-label calibration
Gap It Leaves: No resource/test cost model; Chinese-only data; no safety endpoint

Paper: Evaluating Multi-Agent LLM Architectures for Rare Disease Diagnosis
Stated Limitation: Single model (GPT-5.1); single-turn; marginal gains <2% at much higher token cost
Gap It Leaves: No dynamic topology; no human evaluation; no cost-normalised comparison

Agent Architecture: GP agent + genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, clinical specialists; dynamic KG built with UMLS/MeSH/SNOMED CT
Interaction Protocol: Retrieved subgraph -> contextual prompt -> specialist reasoning
Stated Limitation: KG coverage incomplete; no structured CoT traces; benchmark simpler than real cases
Gap It Leaves: No clinical validation; no cost/latency; no update mechanism for new literature

Benchmark / Dataset: 362 diseases across specialties; automated KG (MedQA planned)
Agent Architecture: GP agent (triage) + specialty agents + automated KG construction pipeline
Stated Limitation: No completed quantitative benchmark in paper; KG quality dependent
Gap It Leaves: No evaluation on standard benchmarks; no cost; no bias analysis

Paper: LLM-based multi-agent system for neuro-ophthalmic diagnosis
Agent Architecture: Information Collection Agent + Diagnosis Agent (LLM ensemble + CNN branch) + fusion
Headline Result: Improves robustness over single-model baselines; preserves diagnostic uncertainty
Stated Limitation: Small dataset; limited imaging; heuristic scoring; no treatment module
Gap It Leaves: No calibration study; no external validation; single author / single site

Paper: MACD: Multi-Agent Clinical Diagnosis with Self-Learned Knowledge
Agent Architecture: Knowledge Summarizer + Knowledge Refiner + Diagnostician agents; judge agent; human oversight on disagreement
Interaction Protocol: Iterative consultation rounds; self-learned knowledge accumulated across cases
Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy; consensus rate; effective opinion rate
Headline Result: +22.4% vs authoritative knowledge; +15.8% vs GPT-5; MACD-human workflow +18.3% vs physicians alone
Stated Limitation: Self-learned knowledge can drift; limited disease set; human study is small
Gap It Leaves: No guideline-version control; no prospective validation; no equity analysis

Interaction Protocol: Guideline-driven dynamic prompting; CoT; self-refinement for disease interdependencies
Headline Result: Beats existing zero-shot methods on CheXpert and long-tail chest X-ray
Stated Limitation: Zero-shot only; no training; guideline text needed
Gap It Leaves: No cross-modal conflict handling; no clinician evaluation; no cost

Paper: MAM: Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Diagnosis
Benchmark / Dataset: MedQA; PubMedQA; PathVQA; PMC-VQA; VQA-RAD; DeepLesion
Agent Architecture: GP, Specialist Team, Radiologist, Medical Assistant, Director
Stated Limitation: No real-world clinical validation; flexible base-model switching untested
Gap It Leaves: Gains measured against weak baselines; no compute normalisation; no conflict reconciliation

Agent Architecture: Multi-role MDT team + lead physician; CorrectKB + ChainKB experience bases
Interaction Protocol: Multi-round consensus aggregation; residual discussion structure
Stated Limitation: Agents are simple; only 2 datasets; dialogue history grows
Gap It Leaves: No cost analysis; no rare/complex disease; no human teaming study

Paper: MedChat: Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Diagnosis
Agent Architecture: Specialised vision models + role-specific LLM agents + director agent
Interaction Protocol: Director coordinates agents; interactive reporting UI
Stated Limitation: No clinician feedback loop; shared prompt causes low output diversity; no notes when unavailable
Gap It Leaves: Single specialty; small scale; no safety/harm evaluation

Paper: MedSentry: Safety Risks in Medical LLM Multi-Agent Systems
Agent Architecture: 4 topologies: Layers, SharedPool, Centralized, Decentralized; 'dark-personality' injected agents
Headline Result: SharedPool most vulnerable; Decentralized most resilient; defense restores near-baseline safety
Stated Limitation: Only 4 topologies; static defense rules; high token cost; no tool/API attacks
Gap It Leaves: No link between safety failures and diagnostic harm; no real patient data

Paper: MeDxAgent: Multi-Agent Consultation for Interactive Medical Diagnosis
Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy; gap closed to full-information oracle
Headline Result: +10.3% over baseline; closes 52.3% of gap to oracle
Stated Limitation: Text-only; patient agent answers strictly from case (no noise); limited sweep of configs
Gap It Leaves: Simulated patient too clean; no test ordering cost; no real clinicians

Benchmark / Dataset: Real-world cardiology patient data adjudicated by cardiologists
Agent Architecture: Multiple fine-tuned LLM agents across modalities + guideline fact-checking
Interaction Protocol: Agent re-examination on inconsistency; report refinement
Headline Result: Outperforms GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-405B, Gemini-pro and BioGPT
Stated Limitation: Small per-arrhythmia samples; subgroup analysis only; single-centre
Gap It Leaves: No multi-site validation; no prospective trial; proprietary data
